matches.quote: The T_C(p) fit has the wrong exponent sign and an unjustified form, and it alone determines the headline p_c. ... The exponent is not motivated
No calculation supports the abstract's statement that the P-3m1 / A-A phase "becomes stable" under pressure... compute the enthalpy H = E + pV versus pressure
the intralayer J1 to J3 are fixed at ambient-pressure literature values... redo the simulations ... with pressure-dependent J1 to J3 and J_L ... and compare simulated T_C(p)
The Fig. 4 caption is garbled ("a) ambient pressure, and a) a lower b) and c) lower than the transition temperature"): it should refer to pressures
The measured R-3 phase fraction does not track the magnetic suppression... plot T_C and M_S against the measured A-A fraction rather than against pressure
Fig. 1: the caption gives the field as 0.1 T, while the panel legend and Fig. 3 say 0.01 T (100 Oe); please correct it
The novelty claim, "first direct experimental evidence" of pressure-induced suppression, should be stated precisely relative to Refs. 18, 20 and 39, which already measured a decrease of T_C
give each magnetization crystal's initial phase fraction, and show whether T_C(p) and M_S(p) depend on it.
The absolute normalization and background subtraction of the DAC magnetization are not described, and the moment-versus-pressure trend depends on them... give error bars on M_S
The method for deriving the R-3 phase fraction in Fig. 5b is not given. The authors should explain how the fraction was obtained
Given that intralayer exchange dominates, the authors should explain physically how AFM interlayer coupling on some interfaces can drive T_C toward zero... with pressure-dependent J1 to J3 and J_L
The P-3m1 subcell does not establish ordered A-A stacking... That is what one expects for random or turbostratic stacking among the three equivalent vacancy registries
The definition of T_C from the 0.01 T M(T) curves (onset, inflection, dM/dT minimum) and from χ'(T) in Fig. S2 is not given
three different critical pressures are compared ... without reconciliation: 6.5 GPa from magnetization at low T, 6.4 to 8.4 GPa from XRD ... and about 10 GPa from Raman
AA and AB "atoms" are distributed randomly site by site (p. 16), whereas stacking faults are a property of whole interfaces between layers
Because the starting phase fraction varies between crystals... give each magnetization crystal's initial phase fraction, and show whether T_C(p) and M_S(p) depend on it.
state which ordered supercell was used in DFT for "the AA phase" and how a structure with fractional Cr occupancy was mapped onto it

notes: The referees reviewed a version with different figure numbering where the M(T) curves were in Fig. S1 (moved to Fig. 1 in arXiv v1, so C2 is fixed_in_v1: true, though the 0.1 T vs 0.01 T caption mismatch in C4 remained). The Raman temperature requested in C6 is explicitly stated as room temperature on p. 4 of v1 (fixed_in_v1: true). For C10, v1 already includes a plot of R-3 phase concentration vs pressure (Fig. 5b), so a reader of v1 does not ask to create that plot from scratch, but P23 and P10 ask how Fig. 5b was derived from the XRD intensities and ask to fit a stacking-fault model to quantify A-A stacking.
